title: Myopia control in children (night lenses, eye drops)
what: The doctor chooses a way to slow down your child's nearsightedness. This can be night lenses, special glasses, or eye drops.
why: When a child is nearsighted and it gets worse year after year.
duration: fitting usually takes 1 to 2 hours; treatment lasts years, with checkups every few months
tell_doctor: How fast the nearsightedness grew and what glasses your child had
How much time your child spends on a phone and with books
What drops or medicines you have already tried

prepare.title: Glasses
prepare.text: Bring your child's glasses and past prescriptions.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Usually the length of the eye and the shape of the cornea are measured. It does not hurt.

prepare.title: Habits
prepare.text: Think about how much time your child spends outdoors. The doctor will ask.

steps: The doctor checks vision and the eye's focusing
The length of the eye and the shape of the cornea are measured with machines
The doctor discusses the options with you
If night lenses are chosen, trial lenses are fitted and you learn to put them in and take them out
If drops are chosen, the schedule is explained
feel: Night lenses can be felt for the first few days, then children usually get used to them
Drops may slightly widen the pupil and make the eyes sensitive to light
after: Night lenses need strict hand and solution hygiene
Take breaks when reading or using screens
Checkups as the doctor schedules, usually every 3 to 6 months
red_flags: The eye is red, hurts, or waters with lenses in: take the lenses out and see a doctor right away
Pus or a white spot on the eye

faq.q: Can nearsightedness in a child be cured?
faq.a: It usually cannot be removed completely, but its growth can be slowed down.

faq.q: At what age can a child wear night lenses?
faq.a: Usually from the age when the child can care for them carefully with a parent's help. The doctor decides.

reminders.text: Myopia control visit tomorrow. Bring your child's glasses and past prescriptions.
